newsitem.title: CANADA: Quorum Growth to privatize itself.
newsitem.headline: Quorum Growth to privatize itself.

text.p: Quorum Growth Inc said on Monday it plans to buy all its outstanding shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange and take the company private.
Quorum said in a statement that it will offer C$8 per common share, first preference share, series 2 and C$0.15 per common share purchase warrant for a total expense of about C$78 million.
The company said the offer will include the payment of the second quarter dividend.
The plan is subject to shareholder approval and will be done through a merger between Quorum and a private company.

Quorum said it will merge with the new private company and exchange shares for new redeemable preference shares, which will be immediately redeemed for cash. The common share purchase warrants will be redeemed by Quorum immediately before the effective date for the transaction.
Quorum said it has retained J.P. Morgan & Co Inc to advise and arrange the financing of the offer through a group of 19 institutional investors, half of whom are existing Quorum shareholders.
Quorum shareholders will be asked to approve the proposal athe annual meeting on May 16, 1997.
Quorum Growth has approximately C$90 million worth of assets under management.
